title.narrative: PESA/ Faso Jege - Pisciculture pour l'Emplois et la Sécurité Alimentaire

description.narrative:
The Fish Farming for Employment and Food Security Project (PESA) was designed and is being implemented by CORDAID’s Country Office in Burkina Faso over a period of six (6) years (2020–2026). The project covers the regions of Guiriko, Koulsés, Yaadga, and Goulmou. It was developed in response to the challenges of employment and food security, particularly for young people and women, in the aquaculture subsector, which offers significant strengths and opportunities. Indeed, the project arose from the observation that in Burkina Faso, domestic fish production accounts for only about 20% of the total fish supply. Fish consumption stands at 7.5 kg per person per year, compared with the global average of 20 kg per person per year, and continues to increase annually. This demonstrates the existence of a growing potential market throughout the value chain, driven by changing dietary habits that favor fish consumption and by population growth. The PESA project aims to facilitate the creation of 1,650 fish farming enterprises, generating at least 2,750 jobs and ultimately producing 600 tonnes of fish. The project seeks to develop entrepreneurial family-scale fish farming, collective fish farming, and integrated agro-aquaculture systems through the promotion of intensive production models that require limited investment and operating costs, both in rural and urban areas. Focused on fish farming for food and nutritional security, the PESA project seeks to contribute to the employability of young people and women in order to promote the social and economic inclusion of these disadvantaged groups in the project intervention areas, including the Goulmou region, through the promotion of entrepreneurship along fishery value chains. In other words, the project will support and promote the development of a robust, resilient, and profitable entrepreneurial family fish farming model. More specifically, the project aims to contribute to:
Increasing the availability of quality fish products in sufficient quantities through an entrepreneurial aquaculture value chain that generates employment and income, particularly for young people and women; Improving access to and utilization of diversified foods at the household level through increased family and collective production, higher incomes, and positive changes in dietary habits; and Promoting sustainable growth and resilience (stability) within the sector through appropriate support services, policies, and governance mechanisms—both public and private.
Through these interventions, the project seeks to strengthen food and nutrition security while fostering inclusive economic growth and sustainable development in Burkina Faso’s aquaculture sector.

The overall objective of the project is to improve the food and nutritional security of populations in the target areas through the development of a sustainable fisheries sector that creates economic opportunities, particularly for young people and women, by promoting entrepreneurship and supporting job creation, which are essential factors for national stability and peace. The specific objectives are as follows: 1. Increase the availability of quality fish through an entrepreneurial aquaculture value chain that generates employment and income, particularly for young people and women. 2. Increase the consumption and utilization of diversified foods at the household level through improved access to fish and positive changes in dietary habits. 3. Support the sustainable growth and resilience of the sector through appropriate support services, policies, and governance mechanisms.
The target population consists of young people, women, and vulnerable individuals.
